neighbours.label: a word that widens a claim to all times, all people or a whole area (always, often, everyone, across the country), as against the same sentence stated about one occasion or person
fire: The staff at the little hotel were always polite to the guests.
The new dance spread across the country in a single summer.
Her jokes delight everyone at the dinner table.
The train from the city is often late on Mondays.
Rumours of the strike travelled across the country by evening.
My grandfather always kept a pencil behind his ear.
The festival welcomes everyone who wants to join the parade.
Winters in the valley are often colder than the forecast says.
quiet: The staff at the little hotel were polite to the guest last night.
The new dance was performed at a hall in a single evening.
Her jokes delighted her brother at the dinner table.
The train from the city was late on Monday.
Rumours of the strike reached the mayor by evening.
My grandfather kept a pencil behind his ear that day.
The festival welcomed a juggler who wanted to join the parade.
Winter in the valley was colder than the forecast said.
